title: Microsoft Frontier program: who in your tenant gets pre-release features?
summary: Hold: Frontier enrolment is not a universal gate, because agents published before 29 March 2026 remain accessible to Copilot-licensed users. Microsoft also documents automation for the Microsoft-built agent access setting and a general Copilot settings audit event, contrary to the page's absence claims.

claims.claim: Frontier enrolment is configured in Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences > Turn on Frontier.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Settings > Org settings. Under the Organization profile tab, select Release preferences. To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On.

claims.claim: Learn documents no PowerShell or Graph call for the Frontier user and group enrolment setting itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Frontier" "graph" "settings" enrollment; "Frontier" "PowerShell" enrollment. Opened get-started-frontier, utcm-copilot-resources (separate OCPS web-app policy), Update-M365UnifiedTenantSettings (no Frontier setting name). No enrolment call found.

claims.claim: An AI Administrator, Security Administrator or Office Apps Administrator account is required to enrol users.
claims.quote: You need an account that includes one of the following roles: AI Administrator; Security Administrator; Office Apps Administrator

claims.claim: The unified release preferences experience is rolling out gradually from mid-November 2026.
claims.quote: The unified release preferences experience is rolling out gradually in mid-November 2026, so it might not be available in your organization yet.

claims.claim: The existing Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier > Turn on Frontier path remains available.

claims.claim: Microsoft-built agent installation is controlled at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agent > Settings > Agent and plugin access > Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft.
claims.quote: go to Agent > Settings > Agent and plugin access. Verify that Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft is checked.

claims.claim: Automation for allowing Microsoft-built agents and plugins is not yet documented.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... areMicrosoftAppsAllowed | Write | Boolean | Indicates whether apps, agents, and plugins built by Microsoft are allowed.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to kind graph, call 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Append to the row note: 'Preview TCM automation: the request body uses mode applyOnce and a baseline.resources entry with resourceType microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes, resourceVersion 1, and properties.valueObject.areMicrosoftAppsAllowed set to true or false.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources. The create-monitor reference explicitly documents applying a baseline in applyOnce mode, not merely monitoring it.

claims.claim: Frontier is an opt-in route to preview Microsoft 365 capabilities before general availability.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Frontier program gives organizations preview access to innovative and emerging capabilities in Microsoft 365 before those features reach general availability (GA). By opting in to Frontier

claims.claim: Frontier covers Copilot agents and other AI and non-AI experiences.
claims.quote: IT administrators can evaluate new Microsoft Copilot agents, review AI and non-AI powered experiences

claims.claim: Frontier features are previews and subject to change.
claims.quote: Frontier features are preview and subject to change.

claims.where: What it is: release audience table
claims.claim: Microsoft's audience-based release model has Frontier, Standard release and Deferred release audiences.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 offers a new three-tier, audience-based release model—Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release

claims.where: What it is: Standard release row
claims.claim: Standard release is the default general availability release experience.
claims.quote: Standard release is the default release experience where users receive new features as soon as they're generally available.

claims.where: What it is: Standard release row

claims.quote: users receive new features as soon as they're generally available.

claims.claim: Deferred release delays deferred-eligible major updates approximately 30 days after rollout to Standard release begins.
claims.quote: Deferred release lets you delay deferred-eligible major updates for specific users for approximately 30 days after rollout to the Standard release audience begins.

claims.claim: Users can be enrolled in Frontier while also assigned to Standard or Deferred release.
claims.quote: You can opt in users to both Frontier preview and assign them to Standard release or Deferred release.

claims.claim: For non-Frontier features, a user's existing Standard or Deferred release preference determines general availability delivery.
claims.quote: For features that aren't part of Frontier, the user's existing Standard release or Deferred release preference determines when they receive features at GA.

claims.claim: Frontier is managed at tenant level by administrators controlling user access.
claims.quote: Frontier is managed at the tenant level. ... IT admins have explicit control which users have access to which Frontier features.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Risks and limits: All users; What to check
claims.claim: After enabling Frontier, an administrator can select All users to give eligible users Frontier features and agents.
claims.quote: All users - All users automatically receive Frontier features and agents. ... After you turn on Frontier experiences for your organization, eligible users can access supported preview features as they're released.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Specific users and groups scopes Frontier assignment to named users and groups and allows a security-group pilot.
claims.quote: Specific users and groups - Only specified users and groups automatically receive Frontier features and agents. ... Use a Microsoft Entra ID security group to target specific users who can access Frontier agents.

claims.claim: Frontier enrolment alone does not replace the licence needed for the product being previewed.
claims.quote: Assign users licenses that provide access to the products you want them to preview.

claims.claim: Frontier agents published after 29 March 2026 are available only to Frontier-enrolled users.
claims.quote: Starting March 29, 2026, newly published Frontier agents are available only to Frontier-enrolled users.

claims.claim: Frontier agents appear in the Agent Store in Microsoft Copilot with (Frontier) in their names.
claims.quote: Frontier agents are available to them from the Agent store in Microsoft Copilot. Search for "Built by Microsoft", and Frontier program agents are displayed with (Frontier) in the name.

claims.claim: Frontier features and agents can take three hours to become available to users.
claims.quote: It might take three hours for Frontier features and agents to be available to users.

claims.claim: Frontier enrolment universally decides whether Frontier preview agents reach users at all, and every agent requires enrolment as well as agent access controls.
claims.quote: Frontier agents published before this date continue to be accessible to all users with a Microsoft Copilot license.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of Why it matters with 'Frontier enrolment controls access to eligible pre-GA features and newly published Frontier agents; Frontier agents published before 29 March 2026 remain accessible to all users with a Microsoft Copilot licence.' Replace its second paragraph's first sentence with 'A Frontier label does not by itself establish that enrolment is required: Microsoft exempts agents published before 29 March 2026.' Replace Governance controls' opening sentence with 'Enrolment and agent-level controls are separate; agents published from 29 March 2026 require Frontier enrolment as well as permission under the agent controls.' Keep the following sentences describing agent controls.

claims.where: Why it matters: factual premise about agents reading tenant data
claims.claim: Frontier includes agents that read tenant data.
claims.quote: Works across Microsoft 365: Autopilot uses authorized Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint information through its available tools.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/autopilot/microsoft-autopilot-application-card to sources. Its Key features or capabilities section supports both factual premises in Why it matters about Frontier agents reading tenant data and taking actions; the current cited pages do not establish these specific capabilities.

claims.where: Why it matters: factual premise about agents taking actions
claims.claim: Frontier includes agents that take actions.
claims.quote: Autopilot can complete tasks without asking at each step. An automated review system reviews each action that sends, shares, deletes, or changes content, or that creates or changes an automation.

claims.claim: The Frontier Get started page does not state whether the toggle is on or off in a tenant that has never changed it.
claims.quote: Searched: Frontier enrollment Turn on Frontier default off tenant release preferences; "Frontier" "default" "off" program enrollment. Opened get-started-frontier and configure-release-options; opt-in steps are stated, but no untouched-tenant toggle default is stated.

claims.claim: A Microsoft Copilot licence is not required to enrol users in Frontier.
claims.quote: With the expansion of Frontier across Microsoft 365 previews to include both AI and non-AI features, a Microsoft Copilot license isn't required to enroll users in Frontier.

claims.claim: Users need a Copilot licence or a licence including Copilot access to receive Copilot-related Frontier features.
claims.quote: to use Frontier features for Copilot, users need a Microsoft Copilot license or a license that includes access to Copilot. Users enrolled in Frontier without a Microsoft Copilot license aren't presented with Copilot-related Frontier features.

claims.claim: Teams-related Frontier features require a licence including access to Teams.
claims.quote: to use Frontier features for Microsoft Teams, users need a license that includes access to Teams. Users enrolled in Frontier without a license that includes access to Teams aren't presented with Teams-related Frontier features.

claims.claim: The Get started prerequisites list admin roles and product licences without naming a separate Frontier fee.
claims.quote: Review the following requirements and recommendations: ... Verify your admin role in Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Assign users licenses that provide access to the products you want them to preview.

claims.claim: Certain Frontier experiences may only be available on a paid basis, so charges are tied to the experiences being used.
claims.quote: Certain Frontier experiences may only be available on a paid basis.

claims.claim: Microsoft refers readers to the Microsoft Copilot Credits Guide for Frontier credit consumption requirements.
claims.quote: Copilot credit consumption requirements are described in the Microsoft Copilot Credits Guide.

claims.claim: Once the unified experience is available in commercial clouds, administrators no longer need a licence including Copilot to opt in through either experience.
claims.quote: Once the unified release preferences experience is available, admins will no longer be required to have a license that includes Copilot to opt in to Frontier via the existing experience or the new unified release preferences experience.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 Frontier FAQ gives a different answer for seeing Copilot Frontier, advising purchase of a Copilot or Microsoft E7 licence.
claims.quote: I don't see Copilot Frontier under Copilot Settings. ... Purchase a Microsoft 365 Copilot license or Microsoft E7 license if you don't already have one. Frontier features are available to all Microsoft 365 customers with a Copilot or E7 license.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe an audit event covering Frontier enrolment setting changes.
claims.quote: Updated a Copilot setting | UpdateTenantSettings | An admin (or system on behalf of an admin) updated a Copilot setting.
claims.fix: Replace the audit-event absence with 'Microsoft documents the UpdateTenantSettings audit operation for changes to Copilot settings; the audit activities table does not name a Frontier-specific operation.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities. Copilot Frontier is explicitly a Copilot setting in the Get started page, so the documented general event's scope includes that existing setting. Remove 'or audit event' from the final Open questions bullet and its assertion that none was found; do not promise Frontier-specific fields or coverage of the new unified experience.

claims.claim: Learn does not document a report specifically recording Frontier enrolment changes.
claims.quote: Searched: "Frontier" "audit" enrollment changes report; "Frontier" "Purview" "enrollment" audit. Opened get-started-frontier and purview/audit-log-activities. A general Copilot settings event is documented, but no Frontier enrolment-change report was found.

claims.fix: Remove the What to check bullet beginning 'Review which AI providers'. It instructs readers to review a control absent from the table. Keep the verified provider dependency warning in Risks and limits; no new control row is required by this correction.
